summary: A particle at the very end of a sentence does not change what happened; it tells the listener how to take the sentence: a yes/no question (吗), 'and what about...?' or 'still going on' (呢), a suggestion or a guess (吧), warmth (啊), 'obviously' (嘛, 呗), 'I assure you' (的), 'things are different now' (了). Decide what the speaker is doing to the listener, then pick the particle.

subs.label: 吗 yes/no question
subs.focus: Decide whether 吗 belongs at all. It makes a statement a neutral yes/no question and must be left out (∅) when the sentence has a question word asking for information, verb-不-verb, or 还是. Classic errors: 你去哪儿吗, 你喝不喝茶吗. Also 吗 vs 吧 when the English is a neutral question with no guess.

subs.label: 呢 in questions
subs.focus: (1) Noun + 呢 = 'and you? / what about X? / where is X?' (你呢? 我的手机呢?); the error is 你吗. (2) 呢, never 吗, softens a question that is already one (question word, A-not-A, 还是). 呢 cannot make a statement a yes/no question: 你是学生呢 is wrong.

subs.label: 呢 for 'still the case'
subs.focus: Statement 呢 = this is how things stand right now, often against the listener's assumption: 在 + verb + 呢, verb + 着 + 呢, 还没...呢, 才...呢. Force 呢 against 了, 吗, 吧 with a clue word (在, 正在, 着, 还没, 才). Classic error: 我还没吃饭了.

subs.label: 吧 suggestion or soft command
subs.focus: 吧 after an action = 'let's', 'why don't you', a softened instruction; 好吧 / 行吧 gives in. The English cue is a proposal or gentle request, not a question of fact. Force 吧 over 吗 (asks if it is true), 了 and 呢. Classic error: 我们走吗 for 'Let's go'.

subs.label: 吧 'I suppose..., right?'
subs.focus: 吧 on a statement = the speaker already believes it and wants agreement (你是老师吧?). English cues: 'right?', 'you must be', 'I suppose', 'probably'. Separate from neutral 吗 by the English; 大概, 应该, 一定 point to 吧. Never 吧吗, never 吧 on a question-word question.

subs.label: 啊 warmth and exclamation
subs.focus: 啊 adds feeling without changing the sentence type: exclamation (真好啊, 多漂亮啊), warm agreement (是啊, 好啊), friendly urging (快来啊). English cue has an exclamation or clearly warm tone. Distractors: 吗 (makes a yes/no question), 吧 (a guess), 呢. 啊 never creates a yes/no question.

subs.label: 嘛 and 呗 'obviously'
subs.focus: 嘛 = 'obviously, after all, you should know' and never asks; the trap is writing 吗, which makes a question. 呗 = 'simple: just do it / so be it', usually ...就...呗, with a shrug. English cues: 'after all', 'of course', 'just ... then', 'so what'. Force 嘛 or 呗 against 吗, 吧, 呢.

subs.label: 的 assurance
subs.focus: Final 的 after 会 / 不会 / 一定会 = calm promise or reassurance about the future (会好的, 他会来的). Force 的 over 了 (announces a change) and 吧 (turns the promise into a guess). English cues: 'don't worry', 'I promise', 'is sure to'. Not the 是...的 past-detail pattern.

subs.label: 了 change of state
subs.focus: Final 了 = the situation is new, not so before (下雨了, 我饿了, 我不去了, 他是大学生了). English cues: 'now', 'not any more', 'has become'. Force 了 against 呢 (still the same), 的 (assurance) and ∅ (plain description). Classic error: dropping 了 from 不...了 'not any more'.

rules.rule: Put 吗 at the end of a statement to ask a neutral yes/no question. Nothing else in the sentence moves.

examples.py: nǐ shì xué sheng ma
examples.en: Are you a student?

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān yǒu shí jiān ma
examples.en: Do you have time tomorrow?

examples.py: tā bù xǐ huan chī là de ma
examples.en: Doesn't he like spicy food?

rules.rule: A sentence that is already a question takes no 吗: not with a question word (谁, 什么, 哪儿, 怎么, 几, 多少), not with verb-不-verb or 有没有, not with 还是.
rules.pattern: Question word / Verb + 不 + Verb / A + 还是 + B + (no 吗)

examples.py: nǐ xiǎng hē shén me
examples.en: What would you like to drink?

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān lái bù lái
examples.en: Are you coming tomorrow or not?

examples.py: nǐ zuò huǒ chē hái shi zuò fēi jī
examples.en: Are you taking the train or the plane?

rules.note: One real exception: when 什么 or 谁 means 'something / anyone' rather than asking for information, the sentence is a yes/no question and 吗 is fine: 你想喝点什么吗? (Would you like something to drink?).

rules.rule: Noun or pronoun + 呢 asks the question that is already in the air about someone or something else: 'and you?', 'what about...?'. With no earlier question it asks 'where is...?'.

examples.py: wǒ hěn hǎo nǐ ne
examples.en: I'm fine. And you?

examples.py: wǒ hē chá nǐ ne
examples.en: I'll have tea. What about you?

examples.py: jīn tiān méi shí jiān míng tiān ne
examples.en: There's no time today. How about tomorrow?

examples.py: wǒ de shǒu jī ne
examples.en: Where's my phone?

rules.rule: 呢 can be added to a question that is already a question (question word, verb-不-verb, 还是) to make it sound thoughtful or less blunt. It cannot turn a statement into a yes/no question; that is the job of 吗.
rules.pattern: Question-word question / A-not-A question / 还是 question + 呢

examples.py: tā wèi shén me bù lái ne
examples.en: Why isn't he coming, I wonder?

examples.py: wǒ men zěn me qù ne
examples.en: So how shall we get there?

examples.py: nǐ dào dǐ qù bù qù ne
examples.en: So are you going or not?

rules.note: This 呢 is optional: the question is complete without it. In drills it is the right choice only because 吗 is impossible after these question forms.

rules.rule: On a statement, 呢 says 'this is how things stand right now', often correcting what the listener assumes. It goes with 在 / 正在 + verb, verb + 着, 还没 (not yet), and 才 (only / certainly not).
rules.pattern: (正)在 + Verb + 呢 / Verb + 着 + 呢 / 还没 + Verb + 呢 / 才 + ... + 呢

examples.py: bié shuō huà hái zi zài shuì jiào ne
examples.en: Don't talk, the child is sleeping.

examples.py: wài miàn xià zhe yǔ ne
examples.en: It's raining outside (you know).

examples.py: wǒ hái méi chī fàn ne
examples.en: I haven't eaten yet.

examples.py: xiàn zài cái bā diǎn ne
examples.en: It's only eight o'clock.

rules.note: 还没 never takes 了, because nothing has happened or changed yet. 才...呢 can also push back strongly: 我才不去呢 (I'm certainly not going).

rules.rule: 吧 after an action makes a suggestion ('let's', 'why don't you') or softens a command so it is not an order. 好吧 and 行吧 mean 'all right then', giving in.

examples.py: wǒ men zǒu ba
examples.en: Let's go.

examples.py: nǐ xiān xiū xi yī xià ba
examples.en: Why don't you rest for a bit first.

examples.py: tài wǎn le míng tiān zài shuō ba
examples.en: It's too late; let's talk about it tomorrow.

examples.py: hǎo ba wǒ gēn nǐ yī qǐ qù
examples.en: All right then, I'll go with you.

rules.rule: 吧 on a statement shows you already believe it and want the listener to confirm: 'you are..., right?', 'I suppose...'. With 吗 you have no opinion; with 吧 you are guessing yes.

examples.py: nǐ shì lǎo shī ba
examples.en: You're a teacher, right?

examples.py: nǐ men yǐ jīng rèn shi le ba
examples.en: You two already know each other, I take it?

examples.py: tā jīn tiān dà gài bù lái le ba
examples.en: He's probably not coming today, I suppose.

rules.note: Never combine 吧 with 吗. A guess with 吧 may be written with a question mark or a full stop, depending on how much the speaker expects an answer.

rules.rule: 啊 adds feeling and friendliness without changing the sentence type: it marks an exclamation (often with 真, 多, 好), warm agreement, or friendly urging. It does not make a yes/no question.
rules.pattern: 真 / 多 / 好 + Adjective + 啊 ; Sentence + 啊

examples.py: jīn tiān tiān qì zhēn hǎo a
examples.en: The weather is so nice today!

examples.py: zhè r de fēng jǐng duō piào liang a
examples.en: How beautiful the scenery here is!

examples.py: shì a wǒ yě zhè me xiǎng
examples.en: Yes, exactly, I think so too.

examples.py: kuài lái a diàn yǐng yào kāi shǐ le
examples.en: Come on, hurry, the film is about to start!

rules.note: In speech 啊 blends with the sound before it and is then often written 呀 (after a, e, i, o, ü: 是你呀, 快来呀), 哇 (after u, ao: 好哇) or 哪 (after n: 天哪). These are the same particle; writing 啊 is always acceptable. 啊 can also make a question-word question friendlier: 你去哪儿啊?

rules.rule: 嘛 says the fact is obvious and the listener should already know it: 'after all', 'of course', 'come on'. It sounds like 吗 but is a different word and never asks a question.

examples.py: tā hái shi hái zi ma bié shēng qì
examples.en: He's still a child, after all; don't be angry.

examples.py: zhè ge wèn tí hěn jiǎn dān ma
examples.en: This question is easy, obviously.

examples.py: wǒ zǎo jiù gào su nǐ le ma
examples.en: I told you long ago, didn't I.

rules.note: After a request, 嘛 coaxes rather than states the obvious: 你就去嘛 (Oh, go on, just go).

rules.rule: 呗 says the answer is simple and not worth worrying about: 'just ... then', 'so be it'. It is casual, comes with a shrug, and most often closes a ...就... sentence.

examples.py: bù huì jiù xué bei
examples.en: If you can't do it, just learn, then.

examples.py: nǐ xiǎng qù jiù qù bei
examples.en: If you want to go, just go.

examples.py: tā bù lái jiù bù lái bei
examples.en: If he's not coming, then he's not coming. So what.

rules.note: 呗 is informal and can sound careless; it is for friends, not for polite requests. Where 吧 would propose something gently, 呗 treats it as the obvious thing to do.

rules.rule: 会 ... 的 gives a calm assurance or promise about the future: 'it will, believe me'. Use 的, not 了, at the end.
rules.pattern: Subject + (一定) + (不) + 会 + Verb / Adjective + 的

examples.py: bié dān xīn huì hǎo de
examples.en: Don't worry, it will be all right.

examples.py: tā yī dìng huì lái de
examples.en: He will definitely come.

examples.py: wǒ bù huì gào su bié rén de
examples.en: I won't tell anyone, I promise.

rules.note: Without 的 the sentence is still correct (他会来) but is a plain prediction; 的 adds the speaker's certainty.

rules.rule: 了 at the end of a sentence says the situation is new: it is so now and was not before. With 不 it means 'not any more' or a changed plan.
rules.pattern: Sentence + 了 ; 不 + Verb + 了

examples.py: xià yǔ le kuài jìn lái ba
examples.en: It's started raining; come in quickly.

examples.py: wǒ è le wǒ men qù chī fàn ba
examples.en: I'm hungry now; let's go and eat.

examples.py: wǒ bù xiǎng qù le
examples.en: I don't want to go any more.

examples.py: tā xiàn zài shì dà xué shēng le
examples.en: She's a university student now.

rules.note: Compare with 呢: 他在睡觉呢 = he is (still) asleep; 他睡觉了 = he has gone to bed (new situation). Verb-了 for completed actions is covered in the 了 topic.

contrasts.why: 哪儿 already makes the sentence a question. 吗 is only for turning a statement into a yes/no question.
喝不喝 is the question. Use verb-不-verb or 吗, never both.

right.py: nǐ hē chá hái shi hē kā fēi
right.en: Will you have tea or coffee?

contrasts.why: 还是 asks the listener to choose, so the sentence is already a question and cannot take 吗.

right.py: wǒ shì shàng hǎi rén nǐ ne

contrasts.why: 'And you?' bounces the same question back, which is noun + 呢. 吗 needs a full statement in front of it.
呢 cannot turn a statement into a yes/no question. It only follows a bare noun or a sentence that is already a question.

right.py: shí jiān bù zǎo le wǒ men zǒu ba

contrasts.why: 'Let's' is a suggestion, which is 吧. 我们走吗? would ask 'Are we leaving?' instead of proposing it.

right.py: wǒ hái méi chī fàn ne

contrasts.why: 还没 means nothing has changed yet, so 了 is impossible. 呢 marks 'still the case'.

right.py: bié zháo jí tā yī dìng huì lái de
right.en: Don't worry, he will definitely come.

contrasts.why: Reassurance about the future is 会...的. 了 reports a change that has happened and does not fit 一定会.

right.py: tā shì hái zi ma bié shēng qì le
right.en: He's a child, after all; don't be angry any more.

contrasts.why: The speaker is stating something obvious, not asking. That is 嘛; 吗 would turn it into 'Is he a child?'.

right.py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù hē kā fēi le
right.en: I don't drink coffee any more.

contrasts.why: 'Not any more' is a change from before, so the sentence needs 了 at the end: 不 + verb + 了. With 已经 the 了 cannot be dropped.

cheat: Question word, verb-不-verb or 还是 in the sentence? No 吗. Only 呢 or 啊 can be added.
'And you? / What about X? / Where's X?' = noun + 呢.
Neutral yes/no = 吗. 'Right? / I suppose / must be' = 吧. Never both.
'Let's... / Why don't you... / All right then' = 吧.
在, 正在, 着, 还没 or 才 in the sentence and things are still that way = 呢. Different from before, 'now', 'not any more' = 了.
'Don't worry, it will' = 会...的. 'After all, obviously' = 嘛 (not 吗). 'Just do it then, so what' = 就...呗.
Exclamation with 真 / 多 / 好, or a warm 'yes!' or 'come on!' = 啊.
